# SpotIt+: Verification-based Text-to-SQL Evaluation with Database Constraints

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#spotit-plus)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.04334v3) · arXiv:2603.04334v3, 11 May 2026; PDF retains an inconsistent FMCAD 2021 template header, not treated as venue evidence

**Reading coverage:** All eleven PDF pages, Sections I-VI, Appendices A-B, equations, Tables I-IV and counterexample listings/figures.

## Research question

Execution agreement on one database can hide SQL inequivalence, while unconstrained formal counterexamples may use implausible domain values.

## Method

SpotIt+ mines ranges, categorical sets, non-null properties, functional dependencies and ordering relations from example data. An LLM filters or relaxes candidates before VeriEQL encodes them in bounded equivalence checking.

## Evaluation

The paper rechecks predictions accepted by BIRD execution scoring from ten systems, with up to five rows per table and a 600-second timeout. It compares no mined constraints, raw mined constraints and LLM-validated constraints, using set semantics.

## What the results support

Constraints alter accepted-pair counts and rankings while still exposing discrepancies missed by fixed-database execution. Worked examples illustrate more plausible categorical values and recovery from overly restrictive ranges; the realism claim is largely qualitative.

## Limits and qualifications

Mined constraints may exclude legitimate future data, and users remain responsible for domain validity. Bounded equivalence is conditional on row bounds, constraints and supported SQL. Reference SQL can itself be wrong. Reported short runtimes concern counterexample generation, not a universal verification guarantee.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Useful for evidence-aware SQL evaluation and counterexample inspection, not standalone request-answerability certification.
